name: yousim
description: YouSim - Identity simulator. Run as CLI or server.
comment:files: Every entry is build output; none of it is in git. `bun run pack` puts it
here: it bundles the launcher into dist/, copies src/web/dist in as
public/, and copies the repo-root README and LICENSE across. Copies, not
symlinks - npm drops a symlink silently when packing, which is how the
web UI went missing from a published tarball. And no lifecycle script may
be added below to automate this: npm copies `scripts` into the packed
manifest verbatim, and packaged.test.ts asserts the published package
comment:deps: No RUNTIME dependencies, on purpose. `bun build --target node` inlines
published package needs nothing at install time and there is no
workspace:* left in `dependencies` for someone else's npm to fail on.
They stay in devDependencies because that declaration is what makes bun
link the workspace members the bundle step resolves through - dropping it
leaves node_modules/@yousim empty and the build cannot resolve them.
npm keeps devDependencies in the packed manifest but never installs a
dependency's devDependencies, so they are inert for consumers.
comment:engines: node >=24 is the floor because storage runs on node:sqlite, the built-in
that keeps this package at zero runtime dependencies. Node 20 and 22 are
out of scope: 22 has node:sqlite but warns and is not the supported
floor. Widening it with a native SQLite package would put a compile step
in front of `npx yousim`, which is a worse trade than asking for a
current Node. Bun is listed too because it is still a first-class
runtime for this package - it uses bun:sqlite instead, chosen by a
conditional export rather than by any code. See @yousim/core's
